mechanical.notes: Budget 45/250 draws (18%), 1180/400000 tris (0.3%). REAL waste removed: this builder was inherited WITHOUT a geometry cache (the other two assets had one from the start), so 44 geometry objects existed for only 16 distinct shapes — the 18 side-vent slots each built an identical BoxGeometry, likewise the 4 LEDs / 3 front throats / 3 lips / 3 blades / 2 rack ears (28 duplicate GPU uploads). Now 16 objects for 16 shapes, cache holds exactly 16 (nothing bypasses), safe because nothing mutates vertex data post-build. Correctly did NOT instance the 18 slots — collapsing to an InstancedMesh saves 18 draws that buy nothing at 18% budget, at the cost of 18 individually-named meshes (shared geometry has no such cost; instancing does). 7 unique materials, no duplicate identical (full-signature compare), art rasterized once, 14/14 named parts preserved, 8 declared groups intact. Offline audit clean (orchestrator-verified: no fetch/XHR/WebSocket/Image/http refs, importmap -> ./vendor/three/). Console clean. CRUCIALLY, the page-boot check STILL passes after the geometry change — an optimization is exactly the change that can kill a page while every module suite stays green, and that hole is now covered.

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. A disciplined optimization: it removed the one real waste (a missing geometry cache the inherited builder never had — 44 objects for 16 shapes) while declining the tempting-but-pointless InstancedMesh collapse that would have traded named-part verifiability for draws already 82% unspent. Right-sizing measured both directions on the screen texture (left alone, in tolerance). No visual regression, offline clean, and — the point that matters most for this pass — the boot check confirms the page still lives after geometry was touched. Cleared to P6, after which the UPS asset is COMPLETE.
